body.translated_text: <s>Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Exposition of the Origin and Analysis of Dependent Arising)

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam | ekasmin samaye bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati sma jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdhamardhatrayodaśabhirbhikṣuśataiḥ | tatra bhagavānāmantrayate sma - pratītyasamutpādasya vo bhikṣavaḥ ādiṃ vo deśayiṣyāmi vibhaṅgaṃ ca | tacchṛṇuta, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasikuruta, bhāṣiṣye -
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, together with a great community of <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), twelve hundred and fifty <s>bhikṣus</s> in all. There the Blessed One addressed them: "O <s>bhikṣus</s>, I shall teach you the origin of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising) and its analysis. Listen to it, attend well and thoroughly, and I shall speak."

body.text: pratītyasamutpādasya ādiḥ katamaḥ? yaduta asmin sati idaṃ bhavati, asyotpādādidamutpadyate | yaduta avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ | saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam | vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam | nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam | ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ | sparśapratyayā vedanā | vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā | tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānam | upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ | bhavapratyayā jātiḥ | jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti | evamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati | ayamucyate pratītyasamutpādasyādiḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the origin of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising)? It is this: when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises. Namely: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations); conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s> arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases); conditioned by <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); conditioned by <s>bhava</s> arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); conditioned by <s>jāti</s> arise <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (old age and death), sorrow, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish. Thus arises this entire great mass of suffering. This is called the origin of <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent arising).

body.text: vibhaṅgaḥ katamaḥ? avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ ityavidyā katamā? yat pūrvānte 'jñānam, aparānte 'jñānam, pūrvāntāparānte 'jñānam, adhyātmajñānam, bahirdhājñānam, adhyātmabahirdhājñānam, karmaṇyajñānam, vipāke 'jñānam, karmavipāke 'jñānam, buddhe 'jñānam, dharme 'jñānam, saṃghe 'jñānam, duḥkhe 'jñānam, samudaye 'jñānam, nirodhe 'jñānam, mārge 'jñānam, hetāvajñānam, hetusamutpanneṣu dharmeṣvajñānam, kuśalākuśaleṣu sāvadyānavadyeṣu sevitavyāsevitavyeṣu hīnapraṇītakṛṣṇaśuklasapratibhāgapratītyasamutpanneṣu dharmeṣvajñānam, ṣaṭsu vā punaḥ sparśāyataneṣu yathābhūta(tā?)saṃprativedhaḥ iti | yadatra tatra yathābhūtasyājñānam, adarśanam, anabhisamayaḥ, tamaḥ, saṃmohaḥ, avidyāndhakāram, iyamucyate 'vidyā ||
body.translated_text: What is the analysis? 'Conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations)' — what is <s>avidyā</s>? It is ignorance regarding the past, ignorance regarding the future, ignorance regarding both the past and the future; ignorance regarding the internal, ignorance regarding the external, ignorance regarding both the internal and external; ignorance regarding <s>karma</s> (action), ignorance regarding its ripening, ignorance regarding both action and its ripening; ignorance regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, ignorance regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, ignorance regarding the <s>Saṃgha</s>; ignorance regarding <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering), ignorance regarding <s>samudaya</s> (the origin), ignorance regarding <s>nirodha</s> (cessation), ignorance regarding <s>mārga</s> (the path); ignorance regarding causes, ignorance regarding <s>dharmas</s> arisen from causes; ignorance regarding <s>dharmas</s> that are wholesome or unwholesome, blameworthy or blameless, to be cultivated or not to be cultivated, inferior or exalted, dark or bright, and those arisen from dependent origination with their counterparts; or furthermore, the failure to truly penetrate the six sense-bases of contact as they really are. Whatever ignorance, non-seeing, non-comprehension, darkness, delusion, and blindness of <s>avidyā</s> there is in regard to these matters — this is called <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance).

body.text: avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ katame? trayaḥ saṃskārāḥ - kāyasaṃskārāḥ vāksaṃskārāḥ manaḥsaṃskārā iti ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations)' — what are the <s>saṃskāras</s>? There are three <s>saṃskāras</s>: bodily formations, verbal formations, and mental formations.

body.text: saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānamiti vijñānaṃ katamat? ṣaḍ vijñānakāyāḥ - cakṣurvijñānaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñānam ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations) arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness)' — what is <s>vijñāna</s>? There are six classes of consciousness: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness.

body.text: vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpamiti nāma katamat? catvāra arūpiṇaḥ skandhāḥ | katame catvāraḥ? vedanāskandhaḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ saṃskāraskandhaḥ vijñānaskandhaḥ | rūpaṃ katamat? yat kiṃcidrūpam, sarvaṃ tat catvāri mahābhūtāni | catvāri ca mahābhūtānyupādāya itīdaṃ ca nāma, tadaikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya nāmarūpamityucyate ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form)' — what is <s>nāma</s> (name)? The four formless aggregates. Which four? The aggregate of <s>vedanā</s> (feeling), the aggregate of <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception), the aggregate of <s>saṃskāra</s> (volitional formations), and the aggregate of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness). What is <s>rūpa</s> (form)? Whatever form there is — all of it is the four great elements and that which is derived from the four great elements. Combining this <s>nāma</s> and that [<s>rūpa</s>] together, it is called <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form).

body.text: nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanamiti ṣaḍāyatanaṃ katamat? ṣaḍādhyātmikānyāyatanāni | cakṣurādhyātmikamāyatanaṃ śrotaghrāṇajihvākāyamanaādhyātmikamāyatanam ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (six sense-bases)' — what are the <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>? The six internal sense-bases: the internal sense-base of the eye, the internal sense-bases of the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

body.text: ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśa iti sparśaḥ katamaḥ? ṣaṭ sparśakāyāḥ | cakṣuḥsaṃsparśaḥ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanaḥsaṃsparśaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>ṣaḍāyatana</s> (the six sense-bases) arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact)' — what is <s>sparśa</s>? The six classes of contact: eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, and mind-contact.

children.text: ) sparśapratyayā vedaneti vedanā katamā? tisro vedanāḥ | sukhā duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā ca ||
children.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> (contact) arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)' — what is <s>vedanā</s>? There are three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, and feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant.

body.text: vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇeti tṛṣṇā katamā? tisrastṛṣṇāḥ | kāmatṛṣṇā rūpatṛṣṇā arūpyatṛṣṇā ca ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> (feeling) arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving)' — what is <s>tṛṣṇā</s>? There are three cravings: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for form, and craving for the formless.

body.text: tṛṣṇāpratyayamupādānamiti upādānaṃ katamat? catvāryupādānāni | kāmopādānaṃ dṛṣṭyupādānaṃ śīlavratopādānamātmavādopādānam ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging)' — what is <s>upādāna</s>? There are four kinds of clinging: clinging to sensual pleasures, clinging to views, clinging to rules and observances, and clinging to the doctrine of a self.

body.text: upādānapratyayo bhava iti bhavaḥ katamaḥ? trayo bhavāḥ | kāmabhavaḥ rūpabhavaḥ arūpyabhavaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> (clinging) arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming)' — what is <s>bhava</s>? There are three kinds of becoming: becoming in the desire realm, becoming in the form realm, and becoming in the formless realm.

body.text: bhavapratyayā jātiriti jātiḥ katamā? yā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmiṃstasmin sattvanikāye jātiḥ saṃjātiravakrāntirabhirvṛttiḥ prādurbhāvaḥ skandhapratilambho dhātupratilambhaḥ āyatanapratilambhaḥ skandhānāmabhinirvṛttiḥ jīvitendriyasya prādurbhāvaḥ ||
body.translated_text: 'Birth is conditioned by existence (<s>bhava</s>)' — what is birth (<s>jāti</s>)? That which, for those various beings in those various classes of beings, is birth, coming into being, descent [into a womb], manifestation, appearance, the obtaining of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), the obtaining of the elements (<s>dhātus</s>), the obtaining of the sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), the production of the aggregates, the appearance of the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>).

body.text: jātipratyayaṃ jarāmaraṇamiti jarā katamā? yattat khālatyaṃ pālityaṃ valīpracuratā jīrṇatā bhugnatā kubjagopānasīvaṅkatā tilakālakācitagātratā khuapraśvāsakāyatā purataḥ prāgbhārakāyatā daṇḍaviṣkambhaṇatā dhandhatvaṃ mandatvaḥ hāniḥ parihāṇiḥ indriyāṇāṃ paripākaḥ paribhedaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ purāṇībhāvaḥ jarjarībhāvaḥ | iyamucyate jarā ||
body.translated_text: 'Old age and death are conditioned by birth' — what is old age (<s>jarā</s>)? That which is baldness, graying of hair, abundance of wrinkles, decrepitude, being bent, being hunched over like a roof-beam, a body covered with spots and dark marks, wheezing and labored breathing, a body bent forward, walking supported by a staff, dullness, sluggishness, decline, deterioration, the ripening and decay of the sense faculties, the aging and decaying of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) — this is called old age.

body.text: maraṇaṃ karamat? yā teṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ tasmāttasmāt sattvanikāyāt cyutiḥ cyavanato bhedaḥ antarahāṇiḥ āyuṣo hāṇiḥ uṣmaṇo hāṇiḥ jīvitendriyasya nirodhaḥ skandhānāṃ nikṣepaḥ maraṇaṃ kālakriyā | idamucyate maraṇamiti | idaṃ ca maraṇa pūrvikā ca jarā, tadubhayamaikadhyamabhisaṃkṣipya jarāmaraṇamityucyate ||
body.translated_text: What is death (<s>maraṇa</s>)? That which, for those various beings from those various classes of beings, is the falling away, the departing, the dissolution, the disappearance, the decline of the lifespan, the decline of warmth, the cessation of the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>), the casting off of the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), death, the making of time — this is called death. And this death together with old age that precedes it — combining both together as one, it is called 'old age and death' (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>).

body.text: ayamucyate pratītyasamutpādasya vibhaṅgaḥ | pratītyasamutpādasyādiṃ vo deśayiṣyāmi iti vibhaṅgaṃ ca iti vo yaduktam, tadetat pratyuktam ||
body.translated_text: This is called the analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) of dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). 'I shall teach you the origin of dependent origination and its analysis' — what was thus stated has now been fully explained.
Thus spoke the Blessed One (<s>Bhagavān</s>). Those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), with uplifted minds, rejoiced at the words of the Blessed One.
The <s>Pratītyasamutpādādivibhaṅganirdeśasūtra</s> (Sūtra on the Instruction of the Analysis and Origin of Dependent Origination) is complete.
